title.en: State the collision theory and the role of orientation

say.en: Hydrogen peroxide sits in a bottle for months, but a pinch of MnO 2 makes it fizz at once. A catalyst does not push the molecules harder; it opens an easier path. In this lesson: Explain how a catalyst works.
State the collision theory and the role of orientation.

body.en: A *catalyst* increases the rate without being used up. It forms a temporary intermediate with the reactants, giving a new path with a lower activation energy. It does not change ΔH, ΔG or the equilibrium constant; it only helps equilibrium to be reached sooner. A small amount is enough, and it cannot make a non-spontaneous reaction (ΔG > 0) happen.
body.kn: ವೇಗವರ್ಧಕ ಕಡಿಮೆ ಸಕ್ರಿಯಗೊಳಿಸುವ ಶಕ್ತಿಯ ಹೊಸ ದಾರಿಯನ್ನು ನೀಡಿ ದರವನ್ನು ಹೆಚ್ಚಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. ಅದು ΔH, ΔG ಅಥವಾ ಸಮತೋಲನ ಸ್ಥಿರಾಂಕವನ್ನು ಬದಲಿಸುವುದಿಲ್ಲ.

title.en: On the board: catalysts and collisions

say.en: A catalyst gives a new path with a lower hump. Start and finish stay the same.
So E a is lower, but delta H, delta G and the equilibrium constant do not change. Forward and backward reactions speed up equally.

text.en: Lower Eₐ; same ΔH, ΔG and K

say.en: Collision theory: rate equals P times Z A B times e to the minus E a over R T.
A collision works only if the molecules carry enough energy and meet in the right orientation.
P is the steric or orientation factor; Z A B is the collision frequency.

narration.en: Reactants must climb the activation-energy hill to the activated complex before they fall to products. A catalyst gives a lower path: Ea drops, so more collisions succeed, but ΔH and the equilibrium constant do not change.

body.en: Molecules must collide to react. The *collision* frequency Z is the number of collisions per second per unit volume. Only collisions with energy at least the threshold value and with the proper orientation are effective. So rate = P Z_AB e^(−Ea/RT), where P is the probability or steric factor. For example, in CH₃Br + OH⁻ the OH⁻ must strike the carbon from the side opposite Br.
body.kn: ಕ್ರಿಯೆ ನಡೆಯಲು ಅಣುಗಳು ಢಿಕ್ಕಿ ಹೊಡೆಯಬೇಕು. ಸಾಕಷ್ಟು ಶಕ್ತಿ ಮತ್ತು ಸರಿಯಾದ ದಿಕ್ಕಿನ ಢಿಕ್ಕಿಗಳು ಮಾತ್ರ ಪರಿಣಾಮಕಾರಿ. P ಎಂಬುದು ಸಂಭವನೀಯತೆ ಅಥವಾ ಸ್ಟೆರಿಕ್ ಅಂಶ.

problem.en: At 298 K, a catalyst lowers Ea by 10 kJ mol⁻¹ without changing A. By what factor does the rate constant increase?

narration.en: Let us solve this together. At 298 K, a catalyst lowers Ea by 10 kJ mol⁻¹ without changing A. By what factor does the rate constant increase?

say.en: Let us solve this together. At 298 kelvin, a catalyst lowers Ea by 10 kilojoules mol to the power minus 1 without changing A. By what factor does the rate constant increase?
k cat/k equals e^(-Ea minus 10 000/RT) / e^(-Ea over RT) equals e^(10 000 over RT).
10 000 over 8.314 times 298 equals 4.04.
e^4.04 is approximately 56.6.
So the answer is About 57 times faster.

problem.en: An exothermic reaction has Ea(forward) = 80 kJ mol⁻¹ and ΔH = −30 kJ mol⁻¹. Find Ea of the reverse reaction.

steps.en: On an energy profile, the backward barrier = forward barrier + |ΔH| for an exothermic reaction.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. An exothermic reaction has Ea(forward) = 80 kJ mol⁻¹ and ΔH = −30 kJ mol⁻¹. Find Ea of the reverse reaction.

say.en: Let us solve this together. An exothermic reaction has Eaforward equals 80 kilojoules mol to the power minus 1 and delta H equals minus 30 kilojoules mol to the power minus 1. Find Ea of the reverse reaction.
On an energy profile, the backward barrier equals forward barrier plus |delta H| for an exothermic reaction.
Eaback equals Eaforward - delta H equals 80 - minus 30 equals 110 kilojoules mol to the power minus 1.
So the answer is 110 kilojoules mol to the power minus 1.
